note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942); the original is in English. The OCR has an extra ".." after the original headline. The original does not describe the worker, so no worker section is given. The type series was taken from a nest inside the trunk of a living black walnut (Endiandra Palmerstoni).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original (Hill 1942) published it as Coptotermes dreghorni, from Timber Reserve No. 263, Queensland (about 5 miles east of Ravenshoe). The alate is very similar to that of C. lacteus and some specimens are difficult to distinguish: the head is usually relatively narrower, the pronotum less narrowed posteriorly, the wings shorter and paler, and the yellowish brown area of the sternites larger; the soldier is a large species that can be distinguished from some specimens of C. acinaciformis and C. raffrayi only by the anterior half or more of the head (above and below) being more or less irregularly stained dark brown. The specific name honours its discoverer, the forester R. B. Dreghorn.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Very similar to C. lacteus; some specimens are difficult to distinguish. The head is usually relatively narrower, the pronotum less narrowed posteriorly, the wings shorter and paler, and the yellowish brown area of the abdominal sternites larger than in the southern species. Antennae 18- or 19-segmented; segment 3 usually very short. Ocellus length 0.11, distant from the compound eye by about half its length. Measurements: length with wings 14.00; length without wings 6.25—6.80; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.43—1.50; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.95—1.10; head width 1.17—1.21; greatest diameter of compound eye 0.31×0.33—0.33×0.36; pronotum length 0.73; pronotum width 1.15—1.19; fore wing length 9.50; fore wing width 2.67.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Large species, distinguished from some specimens of C. acinaciformis and C. raffrayi only by the anterior half or more of the head (above and below) being more or less irregularly stained dark brown. Antennae 16-segmented; segments 3—5 variable, segment 3 usually the shortest. Measurements: total length 5.25—5.50; head length (with mandibles) 2.38—2.45; head length (without mandibles) 1.57—1.65; head length (to fontanelle) 1.39—1.54; greatest head width 1.28—1.32; least head width 0.73—0.80; least width of postmentum 0.25; pronotum length 0.51—0.55; pronotum width 0.95—0.99.
